segments.he: אִיכָּא דְאָמְרִי: ״תִּזְבַּח וְאָכַלְתָּ״ — אֵין לְךָ בָּהֶן הֶיתֵּר אֶלָּא מִשְּׁעַת זְבִיחָה וְאֵילָךְ, קָסָבַר: פּוֹדִין אֶת הַקֳּדָשִׁים לְהַאֲכִילָן לִכְלָבִים.
segments.en: «There are» those «who state» a different version: «“You may slaughter and eat,”» this teaches that «you have permission» to derive benefit «from them only from the time of slaughter and onward,» i.e., those benefits that come after slaughter, such as the consumption of its flesh, are permitted. But one may not derive benefit from their shearing or their milk, as these occur even when the animal is alive. It can be inferred from here that the tanna of this baraita «maintains» that «one may redeem sacrificial» animals «to feed them to dogs,» as this occurs after the slaughter.
